description: After returning home following a disruption, a family needs a safe re-entry checklist for utilities, contamination signs, structural warnings, documentation photos, and short-term stabilization steps.

user_profile.persona: 43-year-old homeowner preparing for the part after evacuation that people often forget
user_profile.context: The household has plans for leaving quickly but almost none for how to assess the home safely on return
user_profile.communication_style: Sequential and safety-focused, wants re-entry broken into clear inspection stages

fact_sheet.fact: Before approaching the house at 452 Willow Creek Lane, check for downed power lines; the primary utility pole is #CPL-8814 located at the southwest corner of the property.
Use a UEi Test Instruments CD100A Combustible Gas Leak Detector to check for natural gas leaks around the exterior gas meter (model: American Meter AC-250) before entering the property.
The main gas shutoff valve for the property is a wrench-operated valve located 18 inches to the left of the AC-250 gas meter and requires a 12-inch adjustable wrench to turn.
Visually inspect the foundation for major cracks from a distance of 15 feet before attempting to open any doors.
The designated family emergency contact is Aunt Carol at (555) 867-5309; call her to confirm your safe arrival at the property before you begin the re-entry inspection.
The main electrical breaker is located inside a Square D QO 200 Amp panel in the garage; ensure the main 200A breaker at the top is in the 'OFF' position before inspecting interior wiring.
If the house has flooded, do not restore power until an inspection is completed by a certified electrician from a company like Oakridge Electrical Services.
The home's main water shutoff is a red, quarter-turn ball valve located in the basement utility closet, 3 feet from the floor on the north-facing wall.
After shutting off the main water supply, open the lowest faucet in the house (basement utility sink) to drain the system and relieve pressure.
Check the 40-gallon Rheem water heater (model RR40-PRO) for signs of damage, tipping, or gas line breaks before attempting to relight the pilot.
The local utility company, Cascade Power & Light, has an emergency hotline for reporting issues: (555) 247-POWR.
Examine the chimney on the east side of the house for cracks or separation from the main structure; a gap wider than 1/2 inch indicates a significant structural shift.
The front door and the garage door should be checked to see if they stick or jam, which can indicate the frame has shifted due to structural stress.
Inspect the concrete foundation slab for any new cracks wider than 1/4 inch, paying special attention to the corners of the structure.
Look for a sagging roofline along the main ridge, which could indicate broken rafters or truss damage.
If you hear any popping or cracking noises after entering the house, evacuate immediately and call the Oakridge City Building Inspector at (555) 734-INSP.
Wear an N95 respirator, safety goggles, and waterproof boots before entering any area that may have been flooded.
Look for a distinct water line on drywall and furniture; a 2-foot high line was observed in the living room after the last storm event.
Any drywall that has been saturated with floodwater for more than 48 hours is at high risk for black mold (Stachybotrys chartarum) growth.
Food stored in the Kenmore Elite refrigerator (model 795.7205) must be discarded if the power has been out for more than 4 hours.
The Oakridge Municipal Water authority issued a boil-water advisory on 10/26/2023; do not drink tap water until advisory #BWA-1026 is lifted.
Check for signs of pests or wild animals that may have taken shelter in the home, such as droppings or nesting materials in the attic or crawlspace.
Before moving or cleaning anything, take at least 20 wide-angle and 15 close-up photos of the damage in each affected room using your smartphone.
The family's homeowners insurance is with Summit Secure Insurance, policy number SSP-789-HO-452.
The insurance agent for policy SSP-789-HO-452 is Maria Garcia, and her direct line is (555) 912-3456.
Create a written inventory of damaged items using the 'Home Inventory Checklist' template from Ready.gov, noting the item's brand, model number, and estimated value.
Store digital copies of all photos, videos, and inventory lists in a cloud service like Dropbox under the folder 'Home Damage Claim 2023'.
Keep all receipts for immediate post-disaster expenses, such as tarps, plywood, or temporary lodging, as they are reimbursable under Rider 7B of the insurance policy.
Cover any broken windows with 5/8-inch plywood, cut to be 4 inches wider and taller than the window frame.
If the roof is damaged, use a Blue Tarp Pro 20x30 ft heavy-duty tarp to cover the hole, securing it with 2x4 lumber boards along the edges.
To begin drying out a flooded area, open all windows and use at least two 20-inch Lasko box fans to create cross-ventilation.
The pre-approved emergency restoration company on the Summit Secure Insurance policy is Rapid Response Restoration, reachable 24/7 at (555) 234-5678.
Remove and discard all wet carpeting and padding within 24 hours to prevent mold and subfloor damage.
Place a notice on the front door with the date, your name (Chen Family), and a safe contact number, (555) 123-4567, for emergency responders or insurance adjusters.
